user.title: Cyber Monitor — NVD API key
user.description:
Cyber Monitor combines CISA/CDC feed monitoring, CISA KEV + NVD vulnerability matching, and network scanning under one integration.

First, an NVD key: a free API key from nvd.nist.gov raises the rate limit from 5 to 50 requests per 30 seconds. Joins CISA KEV and NVD to what your network actually runs, so a CVE is dispositioned against installed versions instead of counted because a vendor name matched. The key is stored in the config entry and never written to a YAML file.

local.description: Home Assistant will run nmap itself. Service and version detection needs nmap's script engine, which this container does not ship — point the data directory at a copy of it, or leave it blank to scan ports only.

reconfigure_local.title: Cyber Monitor settings
reconfigure_local.description:
Change the stored setup values without rebuilding the integration. Nothing here is lost when it saves — the scan history and every device's first-seen date survive.

What you scan and how often are NOT here: those are live settings, edited under Configure, and a copy of them on this form would edit a value the scanner has stopped reading. This form reloads the integration when it saves, because everything on it is only read at startup.

reconfigure_agent.title: Cyber Monitor settings
reconfigure_agent.description:
Change where the scanner agent is and how to authenticate to it. The new address and token are tried before anything is saved, so a typo is refused here rather than leaving the integration retrying with the dialog already closed.

Saving reloads the integration. The agent's own scan targets and timer schedule live on that host and cannot be set from here.

data_description.api_key: Re-checked against NVD only if you change it, so a form opened to fix the scanner address is not refused because NVD happens to be down.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off only for a self-signed certificate on a trusted network.

reauth_confirm.title: Replace the NVD API key
reauth_confirm.description: The current key was refused by NVD, or you are rotating it. Paste the new key below; it is validated before it is saved. This does not touch your scan configuration.

init.title: Cyber Monitor options
init.description: Each of these edits a different thing and saves on its own. Nothing here restarts the integration or touches the scan history — a change is live on the scanner's next tick, within a few minutes.

menu_options.alerting: When a finding becomes an alert

scan_scope.title: Networks to scan
scan_scope.description: Change what Home Assistant sweeps, without rebuilding the integration. Adding a range does not forget anything already found: every device keeps the date it was first seen. A newly added range is swept for liveness straight away; its ports are read on the next scheduled service scan, or now with the Scan now button.

data_description.targets: One or more addresses or ranges, separated by commas. For example 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24
data_description.exclude: Optional. Addresses that must never be scanned, separated by commas. Clearing this field removes every exclusion.

schedule.title: How often to scan
schedule.description:
Two sweeps run on two separate clocks, on purpose. The discovery sweep is cheap and answers what is on the network; the service scan is expensive and answers what each device is running. Running the cheap one often and the expensive one rarely is the point — do not set them to the same figure.

Scanning is checked every five minutes, so an interval takes effect on the next check and is rounded up to it.

data_description.discovery_interval_minutes: How often to check which devices are on the network. Cheap; hourly by default.
data_description.service_interval_minutes: How often to scan ports and identify services. Slow — a full sweep can run for many minutes — and daily by default.
data_description.ssh_probe_interval_minutes: How often to try the SSH key against each host offering SSH. This authenticates against real machines, so a short interval fills their authentication logs. Every six hours by default.

acknowledged_macs.title: Acknowledge unaccounted-for hosts
acknowledged_macs.description: Unknown hosts can never reach zero if one is legitimate but has no way to be marked as fine -- a multi-NIC device (a router, a hypervisor, a NAS with LAG) commonly answers ARP on an interface Home Assistant's device registry does not hold, and nothing here can tell that apart from an intruder without you saying so. List the MACs you have looked at and decided are accounted for; they still show up on the Unknown hosts entity's attributes, in their own list, so acknowledging one is never mistaken for it having disappeared.

data_description.acknowledged_macs: One or more MAC addresses, separated by commas. Any format nmap or the device registry uses is accepted.

alerting.title: When a finding becomes an alert
alerting.description: Two flags — Unknown host present and Actionable vulnerability — and the cyber_estate_event stream behind them are debounced so an automation taking defensive action does not fire on a host that answered one sweep and vanished from the next. A finding is confirmed after it has been seen in this many consecutive scans, and clears after it has been missing from this many. Once a flag changes it is held for the minimum hold before it may change again; a change that arrives inside the hold is applied when the hold ends, and the flag's attributes count how many were deferred. Events over the hourly cap per type are dropped and counted on the flag, never silently.

data_description.alert_confirm_observations: Consecutive scans a host or vulnerability must appear in before the flag raises and the detected event fires. 1 raises on first sight.
data_description.alert_clear_observations: Consecutive scans it must be absent from before the flag clears and the cleared event fires.
data_description.alert_min_hold_minutes: Once the flag changes, how long before it may change again. 0 disables the hold.
data_description.alert_max_events_per_hour: Cap on cyber_estate_event events per event type in any rolling hour. Anything over is dropped and counted in events_suppressed.

error.invalid_mac: One or more of those is not a MAC address. Nothing was saved.
error.invalid_target: That is not an address, range or hostname nmap will accept. Nothing was saved.
